claims.text: The baseline FeNiCrCoCu coating has a relatively coarse-grained microstructure after moderate annealing.
Rapid quenching will refine the grain size of the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Rapid quenching will produce an ultra-nanocrystalline FeNiCrCoCu coating.
An ultra-nanocrystalline grain structure enhances dynamic recrystallization during sliding.
An ultra-nanocrystalline grain structure promotes distributed grain-boundary sliding.
Grain refinement lowers the activation barrier for grain-boundary-mediated plasticity.
Dynamic recrystallization and grain-boundary sliding distribute microscopic deformation more uniformly.
Distributed grain-boundary-mediated deformation suppresses localized shear-band formation.
Localized shear-band formation is typically responsible for increased wear.
Formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface structure is associated with high wear resistance and low friction in a high-entropy alloy under oxidation-mitigated conditions.
Fine-grain strengthening can accompany decreased wear loss in high-entropy-alloy coatings.
The rapid-quenched coating will have lower wear loss than the coarse-grained baseline coating.
The rapid-quenched coating will exhibit a more uniform and less localized microscopic deformation pattern than the baseline.
The predicted wear and deformation changes will hold during sliding at approximately 500–700 °C.
Minimizing oxidation favors dominance of the proposed grain-boundary-mediated wear mechanism.
The predictions require the coating phase composition to remain stable.
A failure to obtain a statistically significant wear reduction or a reduction in shear-band frequency or severity would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as both 'as-deposited' and moderately annealed, whereas the baseline explicitly results from moderate annealing; an annealed coating is not ordinarily an as-deposited state.
